title: Rust Programming
overview: This course introduces Rust, a systems programming language designed for speed, memory safety, and concurrency without sacrificing performance. Participants will learn the core features of Rust, including ownership, borrowing, lifetime, concurrency, and error handling. By the end of the course, learners will be able to develop efficient and safe applications using Rust, addressing the needs of both low-level systems programming and high-performance applications.
audience: Developers transitioning from languages like C, C++, or Python
Software Engineers focusing on performance and memory safety
Engineers building performance-critical or concurrent applications
Developers looking to learn modern, safe systems programming
methodology: Hands-on Coding Exercises – Practical labs with real-world projects
Live Demonstrations – Step-by-step development and debugging
Collaborative Learning – Pair programming and peer reviews
Case Studies & Best Practices – Solutions to common systems programming challenges
Capstone Project – Building a performance-critical application using Rust
competencies: Core Rust concepts: ownership, borrowing, and lifetimes
Efficient memory management using Rust's borrowing system
Writing safe and performant code with Rust
Error handling and working with Result and Option types
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Write safe, efficient, and concurrent code using Rust
Understand and apply Rust’s ownership, borrowing, and lifetime rules
Develop applications with concurrency and multi-threading
Work with Rust's memory management model
Build and debug Rust applications using the Rust toolchain
Implement error handling, testing, and debugging techniques in Rust
